Poulet Nan Sos

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

Serves 6Prep 20 minCook 45 min

Poulet Nan Sos is a traditional Haitian chicken dish served during Fete de Papa Zaka, the Feast of the Farmer Loa, which honors the spirit of agriculture and harvest. This flavorful stew combines tender chicken with a rich, spicy tomato-based sauce, symbolizing abundance and gratitude for the earth's bounty.

Ingredients

  • 3 lbs (1.4 kg) chicken pieces (bone-in, skin-on)
  • 2 tablespoons vegetable oil
  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 bell pepper, chopped
  • 2 large tomatoes, chopped
  • 1 cup (240 ml) tomato sauce
  • 1 Scotch bonnet pepper, whole (optional, for heat)
  • 1 teaspoon dried thyme
  • 1 teaspoon ground black pepper
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon paprika
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) water or chicken broth
  • 2 tablespoons white vinegar
  • 2 sprigs fresh parsley, chopped

Method

  1. Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
  2. Add the chicken pieces and brown on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove and set aside.
  3. In the same pot, add the chopped onion, garlic, and bell pepper. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
  4. Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down, about 5 minutes.
  5. Stir in the tomato sauce, thyme, black pepper, salt, paprika, and white vinegar.
  6. Return the chicken to the pot and add the water or chicken broth.
  7. Add the Scotch bonnet pepper whole to infuse heat without overwhelming the dish (optional).
  8. Cover and simmer on low heat for 30-35 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and tender.
  9. Remove the Scotch bonnet pepper before serving.
  10. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and serve hot with rice or fried plantains.

Tips

  • For a milder dish, omit the Scotch bonnet pepper or remove it early during cooking.
  • Marinate the chicken in vinegar, garlic, and herbs for a few hours before cooking to enhance flavor.
  • Serve with traditional Haitian sides like rice and beans or bannann peze (fried plantains) for a complete meal.
